subject: Physics
description: Temperature scales, specific heat, latent heat, laws of thermodynamics

questions.stem: The TEMPERATURE at which water FREEZES on the Celsius scale is:
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0 °C (= 32 °F = 273.15 K). Boils at 100 °C (= 212 °F = 373.15 K). Conversion: F = C × 9/5 + 32; K = C + 273.15. ABSOLUTE ZERO = −273.15 °C = 0 K (theoretical lowest temperature, no thermal motion). Distractor 32 = freezing in Fahrenheit. Distractor 273 = absolute zero in Celsius (negative).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: SPECIFIC HEAT capacity of WATER (~4.18 J/g·°C) is unusually HIGH compared to most substances. This means water:

options.option_text: Boils at a very low temperature

questions.explanation: High specific heat of water → resists temperature change. Important consequences: (1) OCEANS act as climate moderator (slow to heat/cool); (2) coastal climates milder than inland; (3) water in body helps regulate temperature; (4) cooling agent in radiators, power plants. Sand specific heat ~0.84 J/g·°C — low → deserts cold at night, hot in day. Mostly water on Earth's surface = stable climate. Distractor 1 = opposite of high specific heat.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: LATENT HEAT of vaporization is the heat needed to:

options.option_text: Raise the temperature of liquid by 1°C
Convert liquid to vapour without temp rise
Cool a vapour into a liquid form again
Convert solid into liquid form by melting

questions.explanation: LATENT HEAT = heat absorbed/released during PHASE CHANGE without temperature change. Two types: LATENT HEAT OF FUSION (solid → liquid; for water = 334 J/g, used for ice melting); LATENT HEAT OF VAPORIZATION (liquid → vapour; for water = 2260 J/g, very high — keeps body cool via sweat evaporation; steam burns are bad — releases lots of energy on condensing). Distractor 1 = specific heat. Distractor 4 = latent heat of FUSION (not vaporization).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: FIRST LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS is essentially:

options.option_text: Heat always flows hot → cold spontaneously
Entropy of universe always increases here
Absolute zero temperature cannot be reached

questions.explanation: FIRST LAW = energy conservation. ΔU = Q − W (change in internal energy = heat added − work done by system). Energy cannot be created or destroyed; only converted form-to-form. SECOND LAW = entropy of isolated system never decreases (heat flows hot → cold; you can't make heat engine 100% efficient). THIRD LAW = entropy of perfect crystal at absolute zero is zero (absolute zero is unreachable). ZEROTH LAW = if A in equilibrium with B + B with C, then A is in equilibrium with C (basis of thermometers).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Absolute zero = lowest theoretical temperature. Atoms have minimum thermal energy (only quantum zero-point motion). On Kelvin = 0 K; on Celsius = −273.15 °C; on Fahrenheit = −459.67 °F. Cannot be reached (3rd law of thermodynamics). Closest achieved: ~38 picokelvin (10⁻¹² K, NIST 2003 with rubidium atoms). Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) — special quantum state near 0 K (Nobel 2001 — Cornell, Wieman, Ketterle).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Three modes of HEAT TRANSFER are:
questions.explanation: Heat transfer modes: (1) CONDUCTION — through direct contact in solids (metal spoon in tea heats up); (2) CONVECTION — through fluids (air, water) by bulk movement (boiling water, sea/land breeze, heat radiator); (3) RADIATION — via electromagnetic waves, no medium needed (Sun's heat reaches Earth through vacuum; infrared from hot stove). All hot bodies emit thermal radiation (Stefan-Boltzmann law: P ∝ T⁴). Distractor 1 = light wave properties.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A THERMOS FLASK keeps liquids hot/cold by minimizing all 3 modes of heat transfer. The vacuum between its walls reduces:

options.option_text: Radiation, but not convection at all
All three modes equally well together
Only convection in the surrounding air

questions.explanation: THERMOS FLASK design: (1) DOUBLE WALL with VACUUM between — vacuum has no particles → blocks both CONDUCTION and CONVECTION (both need medium). (2) SILVERED INTERIOR walls — REFLECT radiant heat back (reduces radiation transfer). (3) Cork/plastic stopper — bad conductor. Combined → liquid stays hot/cold for hours. Invented by James DEWAR (1892, Scottish chemist) — initially called 'Dewar flask' for cryogenic research.
